pages.text: What the Precursors left written, as I find it and can read it. Their tablets lie in their cities' archives, vaults, houses and shrines, and in what is left of them in the present: desert and jungle temples, ocean ruins (a brush finds them in the silt), ancient cities, even the chests of villages. The temples of the great beasts have tablets of their own, in an older hand.

pages.title: On the Black Stones
pages.text: The black stones were here before the first city. Nobody raised them and nobody can break them. We have learned one thing about them: near them, nothing goes missing. So we build our shrines round them, and keep our children close to them at night.

pages.title: What Goes Missing
pages.text: It began with a street. Everyone walked it, and one morning no one could remember it being built, and by evening no one could remember it at all. Then a well. Then a name. It is not that things are taken. It is that they were never there, and only the gap is left.

pages.title: The Hand Outside
pages.text: Those who sleep near the black stones dream of something outside all the years there are, working at the stones the way a child works at a loose tooth. It is patient. Where it gets one a little loose, the world near it comes undone, and what comes undone was never there.

pages.title: The City of No Shadows
pages.text: It comes out of shadow. So the Sun Court builds without shadow: white walls, flat roofs, no eaves, no awnings over the streets; lamps lit every night in every window. We sleep on the roofs, in the last of the light. Where there is no dark, it cannot reach.

pages.title: The King's Face
pages.text: There was an eye in the King's shadow. We all saw it, at the feast. By morning none of us could say what his face had looked like, and the painters could not paint it, and his mother did not know him.

pages.title: The Court With No Door
pages.text: Whatever wears the King now must not walk among us. We sealed him under the Court of Noon in a room with no door, and laid fire-powder under its floor, so that if he walks out he will not walk far. Let the sand keep him. Let no one dig him up.

pages.title: Eyes That Do Not Close
pages.text: It cannot take what is watched. So the Tide Kingdom bred Guardians: eyes that never close, all round the rings, under the decks, in the Watch Pools. As long as one of them is looking, the city stays.

pages.title: The Eye Pool
pages.text: The eldest Guardian lives in the pool under the Tidehall and watches the city from below. We feed it by hand. It has never once looked away. The priests say it is tired.

pages.title: The Night They Blinked
pages.text: (stained by water) ...every Guardian blinked at once, the whole sea of eyes. In the morning half the rings were open water, and no one could say who had lived on them. Their ruins lie under the sea, and we cannot remember building them.

pages.title: Down Into the Quiet
pages.text: It finds what can be seen. So the Deep Kingdom went down, under the deep slate, into the dark where nothing is seen, and built our city there in silence. We speak in whispers. We light our streets with soul-fire, low.

pages.title: Guards Who Do Not See
pages.text: We bred the Wardens blind, so that it cannot be shown to them; they know the world by sound alone, and they keep the city. They do not harm us. We grew the sculk to listen with them. Hush near the sensors. Sound carries down.

pages.title: Hush
pages.text: The city empties quietly. A house, then a street, and no one can say who lived there. The Wardens still walk the streets, listening for us. When we are all gone they will still be listening. Do not make them angry: they are all that is left of our watch.

pages.title: The Garden of Engines
pages.text: We do not build machines. We grow them: flesh on brass, under the copper dome. We grew them to remember for us. Whatever goes missing, the engines remember it was there, and tell us, and we write it down.

pages.title: What the Engines Remember
pages.text: The engines remember a street on the east side that none of us has ever seen. They remember a tower. They remember a king. Every year they remember more that we do not.

pages.title: Overgrown
pages.text: Now the engines remember a whole city, and it is this one, and we are not in it. The gardeners say the engines are mourning. To whoever reads this: we were here. The engines will forget us too, and then the jungle.

pages.title: Iron
pages.text: What comes undone cannot take iron. A nail of iron in a doorpost, and the door stays. So the Hearth forged iron watchers, tall as two men, and set them to walk our lanes: our golems.

pages.title: Keep Them Bright
pages.text: Rust is where the unmaking starts: the iron forgets it is iron. Polish the golems every morning. Let no vine grow on them, no flower, no stain. A golem kept bright is a village kept.

pages.title: What the Hearth Will Leave
pages.text: The Hearth is coming undone. Our children will forget the Anvil Hall, then our tongue, then that there was a Hearth at all. But they will keep the golems, and the golems will keep them. Let them live small and safe in little villages. Let them never know what we kept watch against.

pages.title: The Builders' Mark
pages.text: (an older script, the tongue's ancestor) We grew the core to hold this stone still and tied it on with sinew. When the cold comes the cores will die, and the stones will have to hold on their own. Whoever comes after us: watch the stones.

pages.title: Frozen Into the Ice
pages.text: (the tablet is rimed with frost) The core is dead. Its last moment froze around it, and the ice does not melt, for nothing moves in it. The stone still holds without it. Build round the stones. Keep them.

pages.title: The Unmaking
pages.text: The Precursors never knew what the black stones were. They are Nails, holding time in place, and something outside time is working them loose. Where one loosens, things are unmade: not destroyed, never there. Every kingdom kept its own watch: the Sun Court against shadow, the Tide Kingdom with Guardians' open eyes, the Deep Kingdom in the dark with blind Wardens, the Verdant Kingdom with engines that remembered, the Hearth with golems of bright iron. Every watch failed, and the kingdoms were unmade: only their remains are left, and their guards, still keeping watch. The Nails still hold.
